learning: Iteration 5 showed that base_speed 1.5 to 1.3 raised oval progress from 0.710 to 0.884 while the oval finish time held near 1.84 s. The s-bend and slalom excursions (0.0625 and 0.0647 m) remain the open problem. If max_error drops below 0.06 m on those tracks, the controller is the lever and the geometry stays. If it does not, the next step is the wheel_track test the Builder has proposed.
notes: Geometry unchanged from iteration 5 so the controller is the only variable. Lowers base_speed to 1.15 and raises kd to 0.45 to test whether slower turn entry and more damping reduce s-bend and slalom max_error.
rationale: Iteration 5 (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, base 1.3, kp 4.5, ki 0.25, kd 0.40) is the best run so far at 295.09. Oval progress rose to 0.884 with 9 of 20 finishes, and oval max_error fell to 0.046 m. The s-bend and slalom still end off-track with max_error of 0.0625 and 0.0647 m. Their line-loss counts (1.1) and steering oscillation (0.20 to 0.24) show the tape is held and the controller is not jittering, so the excursions are turn-induced transients. Speed reduction from 1.5 to 1.3 helped the oval without costing finish time (mean 1.84 s, well inside 3 s). I therefore apply one further, modest step in the same direction: base_speed 1.3 to 1.15 to lower turn-entry speed on the tight s-bend and slalom, and kd 0.40 to 0.45 to damp the turn-in lag that drives the excursions. kp 4.5 and ki 0.25 stay unchanged so the effect is attributable. The geometry is held exactly as supplied by the Builder, so the controller is the only variable. Expected: oval progress at or above about 0.8, and s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.062 m. If oval progress falls below about 0.65 because the robot is too slow, restore base_speed to 1.3.
